title: "Muhammad is His messenger"
hookLine: the second half accepts the Prophet ﷺ as the one who shows how

lines: NOBODY LEARNS A KNOT FROM A PARAGRAPH.
PRAY AS YOU HAVE SEEN ME PRAY.
cards: Nobody learns to tie a knot from a paragraph. You watch somebody's hands, slowly, then try it, then watch again. The first sentence of the shahadah says there is one God to worship.
It leaves a practical question hanging: fine, but how? How do you pray, fast, treat a neighbor, a spouse, a stranger?
In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gives his companions a short answer about the prayer: pray as you have seen me praying. Watch the hands.

teach.b: Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah. And I testify that Muhammad is His messenger. The Qur'an says it in nearly the same words, in Pickthall's translation: "Muhammad is the messenger of Allah."
First, the word. A rasul is a messenger, one who is sent. Risalah is what he carries: the message, and the mission of carrying it.
Muslims testify that this man was sent, and that what he brought came from beyond him. Second, the message came with a life attached. The Qur'an doesn't hand over a book and leave.
It points at a person: "Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example."
The way he prayed, ate, argued, forgave and grieved became the sunnah, his way, the pattern Muslims look to for living the first sentence on an ordinary day. Third, a messenger and not more.
The Qur'an tells him to say: "I am only a mortal like you." Muslims honor him deeply, and worship only God. The first sentence is about who is worshiped, the second about who shows the way.

teach.h: ONE IN A LINE OF MESSENGERS.
teach.b: Fourth, he is one in a line. The Qur'an names earlier messengers, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and describes believers who make no distinction between any of them. It calls Muhammad the seal of the prophets.
So the second sentence isn't a footnote. It answers the question the first one raises: here is how it was lived, by a man who slept, walked to market, and asked for help like anyone else.

how: Muslims learn the sunnah, the Prophet's way, from the hadith collections and from teachers and parents, and many try to follow it in small daily habits as well as in the prayer.

o: the honor and love Muslims show the Prophet
the holy book, written down by the Prophet himself
the message, and the mission of the one sent with it

p: his way, the pattern to follow

s: the Qur'an has him say he is only a mortal; Muslims honor him and worship God alone.
the Qur'an calls the messenger of Allah a good example
"Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example."
the second sentence of the shahadah is about a book only
it's about a person who was sent, whose life shows how the message is lived.

games.q: the companions want to know exactly how to pray. what does the Prophet tell them?
o: read the instructions I'll write down.
pray as you have seen me praying.
pray however feels right to you.
games.why: Sahih al-Bukhari records it: the prayer was taught by watching him, the way a knot is taught by watching hands.

practice: The hadith collections describe small things he did: beginning a meal with bismillah, in the name of God, and eating with the right hand; greeting people with peace, those you know and those you don't; visiting someone who is sick.
Pick one that fits your day, whether you're Muslim or simply curious, and picture exactly where and when it would happen.

wordCard.voice: Risalah. The message, and the mission of the one sent with it: the second half of the testimony. Today's word.

orig.note: the message, the mission; the one who carries it is the رَسُول (ra-SOOL), messenger.

carryVoice: Your line: he shows the way. The message came with a life to watch. Tomorrow, both sentences, said for the first time.
